Having been dragged into another hobby, this time in 6/8mm scale, and missing models I wanted to field I decided to model my own. As I like my greenskin models a little bigger than usual, they are more like 10mm, but hey - they're supposed to be bigger than usual 'oomies ;)

These have been printed on a resin printer and did fine (as you can see in the images). I include painted versions with the skorchas being WIP, but I will see to that soon.

In the collection you will find:
1. A tank with a long gun, great for laying down direct fire - the turret is separate from the body so you can point it straight in your opponents face ;)
2. A tank with a big gun, for sending shells overhead and smashing multiple enemies at once. There are some accessories added so no two look the same.
3. Two mobile flamethrowers - one 2-nd World War Willis style, the second a tankish ignition machine
4. A big boss on a bike with lots of dakka
5. A regular boss with an equal amount of dakka
6. A BIG WAGON with even more guns. This one has three turrets to choose from so you can customize them to your liking

Update!
7. Added three different leaders in heavy armour and some solid waponry

Built by da biggest Mek around, the Brawla Bot is the ultimate kombo of krumpin’ power and dakka mayhem. Armed with a mix of choppy gubbinz and shooty bitz, dis hulkin' heap of scrap don’t care how it smashes – just that it does.

Whether it’s tearin' through enemy lines wiv buzzin’ blades, or lightin’ up targets from afar wiv loud, rattly shootas, da Brawla Bot is ready for any scrap. It’s got armor thicker than a squig’s skull and enough attitude to make a Warboss jealous.

Designed for tabletop mayhem and hobby fun, dis multipart kit comes with options for both melee and ranged gear – so you can pose it just right before sendin' it into a proper Waaagh!

Note: Dis is a fan-made model, full of grimy character and orkiness, but not linked to any official game or company. It’s just for da ladz who like loud machines an’ big fights.


This model is compatible to the bitz of following models:
- Mosha Bot
- Shoota Bot


======= PRINTING =========

- Layer hight 0.05mm
- Use tree / organic supports.
- I printed my test prints with a 0.25mm nozzle (for best quality)
- Orientate the Exhausts01-04 vertical

======= Assembly =========

If you need instructions - just open all files in 3D Builder or e.g. Meshmixer at the same time (drag and drop). There you can have a look where they need to go in 3D.



---
Shame less beggin' for some coins for caffeine I need doin' stuff like that :-)

Please consider a tip ....this highly detailed model was a work of hundeds of hours of free time!
If you do so, I HIGHLY APPRECIATE YOUR GENEROSITY :-)

Kind regands,
Tersus

Is this a serious release? Not really... Since so many of my 0.2mm nozzles on my Bambu A1 were failing, I thought maybe one could upcycle these as weapons in tanks. And while being on that, I decided to do that for empty ArmyPainter bottles, too. And since I was experimenting a bit with stuff, I decided to try to AI generate three more tanks. So here you are! 5 Tanks that you could play in your games (and I'd be happy if you did and showed me images), but it's quite questionable if you did.

Of course I forged them into a library for my customizer! Have fun combining them with my other scrap tanks!

Powered by Image-to-3D from MakerWorld (https://makerworld.com/makerlab/imageTo3d)

https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/game/y-orc-battle-lorries-8mm-scale/comments#comment-answer-734601

I did these a couple of years ago so I may have forgotten someone's bits: please let me know if so. I'm a bit of a noob with MeshMixer so, again, apologies if for anything messy. I've basically embedded guns in the front, added peg-turrets and given lots of glyph/no glyph [clean] options. They've all printed fine my end so fingers crossed yours. If you have problems with the pegs not fitting the holes properly then just resize the turrets a bit as some resins cure with odd dimensions. These are re-sized to what I think orks should roughly be on the Moonjammy scale (so 90% of Vohvel's originals)? Hope you enjoy using them to munch humies. Waaagh!

UPDATE: 2023-10-11
I didn't expect quite so many downloads so to I've done some extra bits last night that I was going to leave till Christmas. Essentially just some fiddling to create more variety (orks don't really do 'standardised', do they :) ). More glyph options (the numbers correlate with those in JayMull420's pack for those wanting to fiddle more), some new turrets and, crucially, bolted versions of the dozer glyphs in addition to the welded. Hope you enjoy them and any donations to the originators listed above, please, rather than me. Cheers.

This cobbled-together flying piece of scrap metal looks as if it should fall apart under a gentle breeze. And yet, it barrels through the air with wild abandon; bullets, bombs and stranger projectiles flying from it in all directions. A mighty flying fortress, this super-scrap bomber all but ignores incoming fire as it passes harmlessly through open superstructure, or as it blasts away rusty plating that was all but falling off anyway, leaving critical structures safe below layers of bolted on scrap metal.

This 67 piece multi-part kit comes with a huge range of options. It can be built with two wing profiles, alternative hulls with differing tailfins, and a range of options for turrets and bombs, many of which can be mirrored for additional variety / symmetry. It includes monstrous 'bouncing bombs' for some truly 'wild' bombing runs!

The kit is designed to be scaled to 8mm scale model games, such as plane warfare games, or those featuring legions of models fighting. It could also be used in 6mm games where Epic Marines fight in Space, a real armageddon level battle. Compatable with ork style armies, it would be a great proxy for a mega bommber or landa. It is sufficiently detailed that an ambitious hobbyist could print it at 400% scale to create a huge center piece model or terrain for 32mm games set in grim dark universes. This would of course require additional cuts to the model!

I am a hobbyist 3D modeller - not a professional 3D designed. However, this project has taken many, many hours of development, test printing and correction. It is my first 'paid for' model, a reflection of the time it took to create. Almost all my other models are currently available for free, so please do look through those if you are interested in further supporting me and my hobby.

I also welcome feedback and will look to develop this model with improvments and additional options in future.

"'Ere We Go, 'Ere We Go, 'Ere We Go!"
— Common Ork chant heard during a Greenskin WAAAGH!
The Orks, also called Greenskins, are a savage, warlike, green-skinned race of humanoids who are spread all across the Milky Way Galaxy. They share many features with Warhammer Fantasy Orcs (and were initially called "Space Orcs" to distinguish them). They are seen by their enemies (pretty much everyone else in the universe) as savage, warlike, and crude, but they are the most successful species in the whole galaxy, outnumbering possibly every other intelligent race, even Mankind (with the very plausible exception of the Tyranids).

Greenskins are one of the most dangerous alien races to plague the galaxy. Numerous beyond belief and driven always to fight and conquer, the Orks threaten every single intelligent species of the galaxy. Orks are possibly the most warlike aliens in the 41st Millennium, and their number is beyond counting. Amid constant, seething tides of war and bloodshed, burgeoning Ork stellar empires rise and fall. Mercifully most are short-lived, soon destroying themselves in a maelstrom of violence and internecine conflict, but should the Orks ever truly unify, they would crush all opposition.

The Orks' unquenchable thirst for battle has always proved their downfall: historically, the Ork tribes have spent much of their time fighting amongst themselves, waging brutal wars with only the strongest surviving. On occasion, an Ork leader will emerge who is mighty enough to defeat his rivals and unite the warring tribes. His success draws other tribes to him, and soon a great WAAAGH! is underway -- partly a migration, partly a holy war that can exterminate the populations of entire star systems. When the Orks are on the rampage, the galaxy trembles, and in these dark days of the End Time, there are more WAAAGH!s rising than ever before recorded.

There have been woolly, tusked Squiggoths seen on battlefields, but the most common appears similar to a dinosaur. It commonly has a howdah on its back, where boyz ride into battle, shooting mounted guns, such as the Supa-lobba as they go. To protect their "ride", Orks usually add armour plating.

As with all Greenskin organisms, the Magos Biologis of the Adeptus Mechanicus have identified Squiggoth's as fungal lifeforms, though they are fairly rare and can only be grown by the specialist breeder Pigdok of the Snakebites Clan. The size of the Squiggoth is determined by the effectiveness of the feed-formula the breeder gives his creature. Less-effective formulas may result in puny Squiggoths while high-quality formulas will see them keep growing and growing.

Squiggoths themselves vary in size and shape, but there are two primary subspecies:

Big Squiggoths are the smaller but more common breed of Squiggoths, either young or whose breeding and feed were less effective and have stunted growth. They most often travel in packs.
Gargantuan Squiggoths are monsterous creatures the size of a small Imperial Titan, bred from the finest secret feed-formulas of the Snake Bites Clan. They are sometimes the favored steeds of powerful Ork Warbosses.

Here are twelve, perhaps crude, though definitely brutal close combat hand-to-hand melee assault weapons. They are intended to allow give you some extra options and conversion bits for your Chaos Cultists. You do love Chaos Cultists don't you?? Though I think they are generic enough to work for most human sized miniatures in any grim and dark dystopian future setting from undercity gangs, to wasteland scavengers, rebels, organized criminal thugs, and pretty much any kind of poorly equipped ne'er-do-wells up to no good.

Here are the 12 unique weapons:

-- Axe
-- Club
-- Hammer1
-- Hammer2
-- Knife1
-- Knife2
-- Mace
-- Pick
-- Pipe
-- Scimitar
-- Sword1
-- Sword2

Each weapon comes in three STL variants:
1) weapon by itself
2) weapon held in a right hand
3) weapon held in a right hand (hand has a nub to socket into wrists)

Knife1 and Knife2 have four variants each, two with the blade held normally and two with the blade held ready to stab. You can mirror the weapons with hands on them to create left-handed versions. All total that comes to 68 different options. You can use these files for physical or digital conversions as you see fit. They are also Creative Common Licensed so that you can modify them as you please and then share your own innovations.

Enjoy, and may the Dark Gods favor you.

This revised version of my old Autopistol STL has some subtle changes that I like. I also added a few variants with different hands attached for easy conversions. In a grimdark science fantasy universe such a weapon as this might be found in the hands of chaotic cultists, undercity gang members, Imperial officials, militia troopers, organized criminals, xeno cultists, merchants and their guards, household troops, and many more. For physically converting or digitally remixing miniatures this one pistol has many potential uses.

I made some changes to my existing Autopistol Model 302 STL. I took most of my inspiration for the original design from a couple images I found online. I liked the look overall, though I felt like the end of the barrel was maybe inclined to break off if dropped. So for this version I changed the proportions so that the muzzle break in front of the weapon connected very slightly to the angled front of the forward handgrip on the pistol. Looking at other images online, I also decided to shorten the pistol's ammo magazine. Previously the magazine extended below the pistol grip, but now it stops just short of being equal in length to the pistol grip. The width and height of the pistol remain the same, but I shortened the overall length from 12mm to 11.5mm which I think makes it scaled a bit better for most plastic, resin, and STL miniatures out there.

Here's a link to the original version.

Autopistol - Model 302 -by- Scavvon
https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/game/autopistol-model-302

When building Gore Krusha Mega Walkers, greenskin Meks sometimes opt to build massive klanky klaws as melee weapons instead of the often-seen giant saws.


FOR BEST QUALITY PRINT, PLEASE READ ALL(!) OF BELOW:

This highly detailed Klaw Arm is compatible to my Gore Krusha's Mega Walker
https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/game/gore-krusha-mega-walker

I REALLY recommend a layer high of 0.050 or lower for all parts to get the quality I intended.
Please see the pics of my print, those are all in FDM (0,05mm layer height)!

I tried to keep the need of tree supports low, but I recommend it to use them on some parts - decide for yourself & make sure to set the tree support z-distance to a multiple of 2 (layer height) for optimal removal (keep in mind: layer height 0.05 to 0.075(!) )


----------------------------------------------------------------------
-------------- EXCEPTIONAL 'fings for this model: --------------------
----------------------------------------------------------------------

---------- MOVABLE PARTS ----------
- Most pivot points are actually functional, pose the arm as you want!
- I have included a functional hydraulics option for the klaw, so it can move once assembled.
 -> You need a well calibrated printer to get this hydraulics working. Print all *FlexHydraulics*.stl with wallcount = e.g. 99 to get a massive print without infill.
 -> For the FlexHydraulics pins you need to cut of ca. 10mm of regular 1,75mm filament. (I did not test this in resin, but I guess you could print them)
 -> As an option to the FlexHydraulics there are two fixed versions. Have a look in the parts.
- Print all PINS with wallcount = e.g. 99 to get a massive print without infill.

---------- CABLES and WIRES ----------

KlawArm_03 Bits come with an option to glue in some wires (or filament).
If you use some 0,75mm² or 0,5mm² electrical wires the arm could still be movable :)

---------- Arm on the LEFT or RIGHT? ----------
You can print all parts normally except the shoulder pauldrons. (because of the flat printing side)
-> You have to mirror both pauldrons if you want the arm on the left side of your model (from your point of view)

---------- ASSEMBLY ----------

If you need instructions - just open all files in 3D Builder or e.g. Meshmixer. There you can look where they need to go.

---------- FOLLOWING: ----------

Shame less beggin' for some coins for caffeine I need doin' stuff like that :-)

Please consider a tip ....this highly detailed model was a work of 80h+ of free time!
If you do so, I HIGHLY APPRECIATE YOUR GENEROSITY :-)

Kind regards,
Tersus

Quite a bit larger than an Imperial Baneblade, a Kill Grinda Mega Fortress is truly a fearsome idol of the brutish Ork gods:
On massive, krushin' trakks, armed with weapons capable of destroying entire hab blocks with one shot, they rumble onwards, where da fORKtress Kaptains points them to.
Only the most powerful Warbosses have 'nuff teef to pay the bestest meks to build these mega-super-heavy assault vehicles.

An IMPORTANT note for the scale :D
- Quote of an imperial agent during a massive Ork encounter on Fungusius Primus:
"Big Mek Gutgrinda once build this thing at a scale of a Baneblade (~79%).... he was KRUSHED and GRINDED brutally to deff by WAAAGHBOSS Gobba Gitkrusha's 'GORKAfORKress' (100% scale)" ;-)



----------------------------------------------------------------------
------- FOR BEST PRINT QUALITY , PLEASE READ ALL(!) OF BELOW: --------
----------------------------------------------------------------------

I REALLY recommend a layer hight of 0.075 or lower for all parts to get the quality I intended.
Please see the pics, those are all printed in FDM (<=0,075mm)!

All parts are printed without tree supports, some parts don't need supports, but please decide for your self. :)

----------------------------------------------------------------------
---------------- EXCEPTIONAL 'fings for this model: ------------------
----------------------------------------------------------------------

---------- Over all printing recommendation! ----------

Many parts have a "flat surface" -> face those to the build plate. Keep in mind, the z-axies does the detailed job!
Detailed sides / most visible sides should be faced towards the cooling fan.

The supa gattla can fit two 5x3mm magnet to be rotatable. The "KillGindaMegaFortress_SupaGattla_Pin.stl" does a similar job, but not as good, I guess... although I never tested the magnets.

The main gun can be assembled in 3 ways:
- Mega Zzappa
- Nukular Shell (with or without spacer, as you like)
- None of both

I printed the supa gattla ammo without a raft, but if you have problems with adhesion, use a raft.
-> If you have concerns about the sharp corners of the ammo belt in FMD, you have the right feeling, but "in the end it doesn't matter", you will not see this issue after assembly.
-> enable "print thin walls" in cura or equivalent in your slicer.

Arrange the lobbas ("KillGrindaMegaFortress_Lobbas02 - 07 & _LazerMarker) as you like, view all files in e.g. 3D Builder or Meshmixer to see how I designed them. The "Lazer sight"-bit is optional, you can replace it with an additional lobba as you like.

---------- Assembly ----------

All parts have a arritation point, so just "move" them until they snap or feel right.
- If you need instructions: just open all files in 3D Builder or e.g. Meshmixer. There you can look where all parts belong to.


---------- FOLLOWING: ----------

Shame less beggin' for some coins for coffein I need doin' stuff like that :-)

Please consider a tip ....this highly detailed model was a work of 100h+ of free time!
If you do so, I HIGHLY APPRECIATE YOUR GENEROSITY :-)

Kind regards,
Tersus

Want to fire some flesh eatin' short range artillery ammunishun that's not a bug?? Rukka Buggys are your vehicle of choice! Slap it! Expolode it!
"How much bity or 'splodin' flesh balls you want to shoot??" - "Yes."


FOR BEST QUALITY PRINT, PLEASE READ ALL(!) OF BELOW:

To print the Rukka Buggy, you need time or a resin printer ;-)
I REALLY recommend a layer high of 0.075mm or lower for all parts to get the quality I intended.
Please see the pics, those are all printed in FDM (<=0,075mm)!

I highly recommend it to use tree supports (at least on the crew) - make sure to set the tree support z-distance to a multiple of 2 (layer hight) for optimal removal (keep in mind: layer hight 0.05 (crew) or 0.075mm (buggy))

---------- Over all printing recommendation (FDM) ----------

- Many parts have a flat surface -> face those to the build plate. Print slow (25mm/s)
- Detaild sides / most visible sides should be faced towards the cooling fan.
- Crew should be printed with tree supports, rotated 45° back (so the face is up). Support Z-distance should be a multiple of 2 to 3 of the layer hight (0.05 - 0.075mm). PRINT SLOW - Outer wall max 25mm/s. You want dem details gooood!

The most difficult parts (actually not the Gobbo Crew...):
- "RuckaBuggy_Rear_02.stl": you need to be super carefull to remove tree supports (they are needed). My test print broke on the bars while removing them. I was able to glue it back on (tip: smooth cracks with a lighter)
- "RuckaBuggy_Front_04.stl": failed 4 times while removing tree supports, combined with other parts. I needed to print this part as a single part with normal supports.

---------- Assembly ----------

If you need instructions - just open all files in 3D Builder or e.g. Meshmixer. There you can look where they go.
Some parts are press fits (e.g. the wheels) you don't need to glue them, unless you print in resin (not tested).
I recommend to "dry fit" the parts with blu tack or a similar reusable putty.


---------- FOLLOWING: ----------

Shame less beggin' for => "Tossin' a coin to your Tersus...." :D

Please consider a tip ....this highly detailed model was a work of many hours of free time!
If you do so, I HIGHLY APPRECIATE YOUR GENEROSITY :-) :-) :-)

Kind regards,
Tersus

FOR BEST QUALITY PRINT, PLEASE READ ALL(!) OF BELOW:

"GorkaBot_Belly.stl" prints without tree support! Just use regular supports.

The doors should be printed without supports with a brim (see Cura screenshot)





---------- LEGS ----------





The legs are unique, there is an individual model for the right / left leg. Those are mirrorable / interchangeable if you want.





---------- ARMS----------





The arms should fit 10x4mm magnets (not tested) but also have a ball joint for more posability...





The "GorkaBot_Klaw_Arm_02.stl" should be printed 45° "floating 1,5mm in the air" see my Cura screenshot - this will give you the best quality result!

Plasma weapons are extremely effective at close to medium range. Together with kinetic damage, it transfers significant thermal damage to the target. At close range, this weapon has a chance to damage even heavy armored vehicles. During the Last War, plasma weapons were widespread among the Shapers.

Despite its high efficiency, this weapon has its drawbacks. The lethality of the weapon decreases significantly with distance. The design of this weapon is quite complex, which requires a high production culture and careful maintenance. And in case of malfunctions, self-detonation of the weapon is quite possible.

Cumulative and armor-piercing ammunition can easily cope with light enemy vehicles. Ammunition with programmable detonation will not leave any chance for the infantry, even in cover.

However, this weapon also has a number of disadvantages. It is quite heavy and for long-term use it is necessary to have exo-armor or genetic modifications. It is also extremely ineffective at close ranges, since the ammunition does not have time to pick up the required speed.

The weapon can be equipped with various magazines. To improve the accuracy of fire, it is possible to install an elongated barrel. Installation of an optical sight is also possible.

The Skrappin' Mega Bot is a stompin' armored Mech capable of moving objects without any efforts using it's powerfull trakktor kannon! Dead 'ard

killy saws tear apart every enemy getting to close. Once the Skrappin' Mega Bot krushed some enemy vehicles, turing those into piles of skrapp, it 

can do some quick n' dirty fixin' jobs on allied vehicles or mechs.


FOR BEST QUALITY PRINT, PLEASE READ ALL(!) OF BELOW:

Beneath my Krumpin' Mega Bot this is one of my most detailed models until now!

To print this monster, you need time or a resin printer ;-)
I REALLY recommend a layer high of 0.075 or lower for all parts to get the quality I intended, while designing this model - please see the pics, those

are printed in FDM (<=0,075mm)!

I tried to keep the need of tree supports low, but I highly recommend it to use them - make sure to set the tree support z-distance to a multiple of 2

(layer hight) for optimal removal (keep in mind: layer hight 0.05 to 0.075(!) )

For a few bitz I added a resin version with "_Resin" in the file name - unlike the FDM versions those don't have a flat bottom. (I have not test printed 

these files, but they should be good to go!)

The Trakktor Kannon can be a variant of an actuall (rattling) Kannon, as it lifts up 'eavy objects and throw them with a high velocity to enemy gitz - 

less explosiv, more smashin' - same damage! ;-)

----------------------------------------------------------------------
---------- EXCEPTIONAL 'fings for this model: ----------
----------------------------------------------------------------------


---------- COMPATIBILITY ----------

Most parts are compatible to my Krumpin' Mega Bot, so you can build your variant as you like :)
https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/game/krumpin-mega-bot

---------- MAIN BODY ----------

You CAN use two 10x4mm Neodym magnets for the junction "hip <> main hull" to get a rotatable/removable body!
As an alternative to the magnets print the file "ScrappinMegaBot_Hip02.stl"

---------- LEGS ----------

The legs are unique, there is a individual model for the right / left leg. Those are mirrorable / interchangeable if you want.

---------- Over all printing recommendation! ----------

Many parts have a "flat surface" - face those to the build plate.

---------- FOLLOWING: ----------

Shame less beggin' for some coins for coffein I need doin' stuff like that :-D ;-)

Please consider a tip ....this HIGH detailed model was a work of 80h+ of free time!
This model is not a simple remix, all parts of my Krumpin' Mega Bot have been reviewed and altered with new details! :-)
If you do so, I HIGHLY APPRECIATE YOUR GENEROSITY :-) :-):-)

Kind regards,
Tersus

Designed up this dealer button to use in home games or have just as something laying around for any poker fan. It was inspired by a dealer button in Pokerstars VR.

Printing:

Ring - Infil to add weight, supports needed for spade inset. Letter embossing doesn't need it.
Spade - Infil to add weight, no supports
Letters - Print flat, already scaled to fit nicely in the embossing
Star - Infil to add weight.

Full print with 4x4x4 walls/top/bottom and 38% infil came to about 48g in weight.

Glue in lettering and spade. Star may need minor sanding but should push fit into the space tightly and not need anything else to secure it.

UPDATE: Found there was some geometry present in heads 1 and 2 for each type that may present problems, so I went through and cleaned it out. If you printed these with resin before, should be wary of little pockets of resin within the mouth. New ones do not have these voids.

There are a lot of orcish heads about this website, but I wanted to make my own. I started by putting together some shapes, mostly toruses and squished spheres, in the general form I wanted compared to available orcish heads, and then sculpted the finer details, until I was happy enough to make multiple expressions from it.

I couldn't settle on a specific nose or teeth type, so I decided to use both in extra combos with all the facial expressions I sculpted, resulting in twenty, 20, different head combinations.

I wanted something that could be used for a number of orcish plans I have coming up, something that could work for more warfam figures that I may produce. Panzerfauste, the fantasy ww2 with british orcs, is a game these could be used for.

Have fun with them and be creative all!

The Krumpin' Mega Bot is a hulking, heavily armored monster! Pistons, welded to powerful close combat weapons, such as the Ripper Klaw deliver enormous hydraulik power to every git or vehicle gettin' to close.
Other than the more commonly Deff Bots and or Kans, Krumpin' Mega Bots are usually armed with high speed rattling weapons of high calibers to kill enemies even before reaching them in close combat! (Or just to make horrible loud noise...)

EDIT: Most Parts are compatible to my Skrappin' Mega Bot
https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/game/skrappin-mega-bot
Build your Bot as you like! :-)

FOR BEST QUALITY PRINT, PLEASE READ ALL(!) OF BELOW:

This is my ambitious model until now!

To print this monster, you need time or a resin printer ;-)
I REALLY recommend a layer high of 0.075 or better for all parts to get the quality I intended, while designing this model - please see the pics, those are printed in FDM

(<=0,075mm)!

I tried to keep the need of tree supports low, but I highly recommend it to use tree supports - make sure to set the tree support z-distance to a multiple of 2 for optimal removal

(keep in mind: layer hight 0.05 to 0.075(!) )

For the Rippa Klaw I added a resin version with "_Resin" in the file name - unlike the FDM versions those don't have a flat bottom. (I have not test printed these files, but they

should be good to go!)

----------------------------------------------------------------------
---------- EXCEPTIONAL 'fings for this model: ----------
----------------------------------------------------------------------


---------- GUN ARM: ----------

THE RATTLA KANNON MAGAZINE IS ROTATABLE IF DONE AS INTENDED!!

For the axies you simply insert usual filament!
If you don't glue the "MegaBot_RattlerKannon_06.stl" to "...05.stl" the "MegaBot_RattlerKannon_Mag.stl" is interchangeable - who knows what might be released in future...... ;-)
-> If you don't want this or don't have filament, just glue the parts as wanted.


Assembly as followed: (please see also the last two pics/screenshots!

1. Stick (NOT glue, if you want it to be removable) together:
"MegaBot_RattlerKannon_05" & "MegaBot_RattlerKannon_06", OPTIONAL: "MegaBot_RattlerKannon_Barrel.stl"

2. Insert a 1.75mm filament (42mm long - as the answer to all questions, lol) into "MegaBot_RattlerKannon_Mag_Back_Spacer.stl", large side first, followed by

"MegaBot_RattlerKannon_Mag".

2.a) Glue on all parts of "MegaBot_RattlerKannon_Mag_Back.stl", if you want more realistic details (even if Ork xD).
2.a.note: Warning: print "MegaBot_RattlerKannon_Mag_Back.stl" with "brim" 3mm+.
They will, regardless of brim width, fall apart after removing the brim. This is intended so you can glue them bitz more random on the Mag!

3. "Dry fit" (NO glue at first!) all parts

3.a) View the last two pics (Tinkercad screenshots)!

3.b) "MegaBot_RattlerKannon_Trigger.stl" to
 "MegaBot_RattlerKannon_Mag_Back_Spacer.stl"

3.c) I recommend to glue in "MegaBot_RattlerKannon_TriggerPin.stl" to "MegaBot_RattlerKannon_Trigger.stl" first.

3.d) Glue the filament between "MegaBot_RattlerKannon_Trigger.stl" & "MegaBot_RattlerKannon_Mag_Back_Spacer.stl"


---------- MAIN BODY ----------

You CAN use two 10x4mm Neodym magnets for the junction "hip <> main hull" to get a rotatable/removable body!

---------- LEGS ----------

The legs are unique, there is a individual model for right / left leg. Those are mirrorable / interchangeable.

---------- Over all printing recommendation! ----------

Many parts have a "flat surface" - face those to the build plate.


---------- FOLLOWING: ----------

Shame less beggin' for some coins for coffein I need doin' stuff like that :-D ;-)

Please consider a tip ....this HIGH detailed model was a work of 100h+ of free time (~50 RL days)! If you do so, I HIGHLY APPRECIATE YOUR GENEROSITY :-) :-):-)

Kind regards,
Tersus

This is a Curtiss-Wright J2 Fury from the game Crimson Skies. **This version is bigger than game pieces and has a little more detail, the idea is to print it to be used as desktop token just for Crimson Skies fans**

**Remember you can leave a tip for the zeppelin crew here: [Beer for the crew](https://www.paypal.com/paypalme/toposolitario)**

Creating Crimson Skies planes for 3D printing is something that no-one has done previously. And it is a shame as the planes are pretty iconic and after many years from it discreet publishing, FASA's Crimson Skies still has a lot of fans who play or are willing to play from time to time.

I started this for testing the VR modelling tool Gravity Sketch, and I found that work flow is so quick that a new plane can be created from zero in almost an hour. First I made the Fury (the one I like most), and the results for it and the Peacemaker were so good that I finally am willing to complete the full series (basic box plus the Balmoral).

In the end... I'll have a good bunch of pieces just to frankenbuild almost any flying perversion just by dragging and dropping! XD

It is not designed to be printer friendly, but it is coming out perfect with resin printers and pretty good in FDM (I suggest to print them vertically with supports growing from the tail).

*Honk if you're a Crimson Skies fan!!*

This is the Ravenscroft Coyote from the game Crimson Skies.

**Remember you can leave a tip for the zeppelin crew here: [Beer for the crew](https://www.paypal.com/paypalme/toposolitario)**

Creating Crimson Skies planes for 3D printing is something that no-one has done previously. And it is a shame as the planes are pretty iconic and after many years from it discreet publishing, FASA's Crimson Skies still has a lot of fans who play or are willing to play from time to time.

I started this for testing the VR modelling tool Gravity Sketch, and I found that work flow is so quick that a new plane can be created from zero in almost an hour. First I made the Fury (the one I like most), and the results for it and the Peacemaker were so good that I finally am willing to complete the full series (basic box plus the Balmoral).

In the end... I'll have a good bunch of pieces just to frankenbuild almost any flying perversion just by dragging and dropping! XD

It is not designed to be printer friendly, but it is coming out perfect with resin printers and pretty good in FDM (I suggest to print them vertically with supports growing from the tail).

*Honk if you're a Crimson Skies fan!!*

"Each crackle of their rifles, was a death sentence to their enemies. Their old rifles had been replaced for this mission, and the soldiers had been eager to try out the fresh forge-crafted laser rifles. The normal magazines had been exchanged for a power cable, hooked up to the proto-fusion capacitators on their back; standard issue for their regiment; allowing them a much higher rate of fire, and fewer reloads than normal"

3 different variants of snipers intended for 28mm wargaming, in line with the rest of the Hostile Environment Guardsmen I've made, and also includes a standalone sniper rifle. Due to popular requests, I made sure that the cables were much thicker and wider this time, to make them easier for printing and painting.
This is also one of the few times I'll be using legs (by ZioCru, go check out his stuff), as I intend for the models I make to be used as conversion pieces, and not wholly printed models.

Enjoy!

I spent an ungodly amount of time in TinkerCAD modifying the original parts to print easier and allow more options.

Rigged version of an ork made by VidovicArts. I used this to create all my ork models so far.

There are a some hidden parts in the file and lots of poses in the pose library of the rig. My workflow with this is as follows:

-Add objects like torsi an weapons to the file an pot them to the right place at the body
-hide all parts you don't need for your boi
-make copy of the rig, the body and all parts you added
-parent all objects to the rig (as objects to specific bones)
-choose a pose from the pose library or create a new one.
-apply all modifiers to the parts
-unparent all objects while keeping their transformation
-boolean unite all objects
-use windows 3D builder to repair any problems in the mesh
-print

Der wer big oh-gerz on this world and da grots stole der bins fer der tank turrets. Who sez any ol rubbish makes good shooty tank turrets iz right.

Idea was using a trashcan turret similar to the early scorcher model. If you want me to make it smaller I can do so by making a reducer ring to the turret adapter on the tank bodies. Aim is to eventually enhance the variability of grot tanks and to offer more bits for future kit bashing. Turret can be used with or without the mantle section.

Turret taken from Trash can with removable lid by Woodmore would fit Grot Tank and Grot Walking Tank by AgentSmith99. Made some weapons available to fit from gaming tank cannon collection by bulldog2708. Alt turret hatch was 28mm tank hatch (open and closed) by Forpost_D6 and Ork Skull Glyph was from 40K Ork Symbols
by kombatunit.

These fit to the Grot Tank design by AgentSmith99. Only used this design for measuring where the holes need to be. Cogs, Gears and Sprockets Group 1 by EpicNameFail are perfect for adding hubs to wheels, etc.

Please note that track section may be a little tight to fit initially. i thought better tight than too loose.

Now added a single track section. These are best joined up before printing if you need small lengths of track.

Big props to the originators of the files i remixed from!

These are conversion parts for turning regular Intercessors into Suppressors.

I like the idea of what Suppressors can do but not how the official models look, super unwieldy guns, grav/jump packs not looking jump-packy enough, odd moon boots.
(and those models are only available in a boxed set that also containing lots of stuff im not interested in) .

After looking at some conversions and kitbashes i decided to try doing a remix that would be more to my taste, this is what i came up with.

To use this one needs to cut away the Bolt Rifle from the right hand and scoop material out of the left hand to fit the handle (or replace said hand with an empty bolter left from a previous marine kit).

Ive used Dark Imperium Intercessors for mine but these parts should be usable on pretty much any of the Intercessor models holding their bolter with both hands.

Suppressors go on 40mm bases, here is one: https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:3312581

From behind a dense copse of trees, a large shape trundles forth. It sniffs and bends down, broad nose pushing through the detritus of the forest floor, searching for something. Its dense, earthy fur is entwined with a dense mat of hyphae, and you're not entirely sure where it begins and ends, all seemingly connected to the odd collection of mushrooms fruiting over its body. It looks up, chewing absentmindedly on something, stopping suddenly as it notices your party. It eyes you warily, snorting loudly in your direction, before bolting back into the forest's depths, a dense cloud of spores swirling behind it.


This is what happens when hungry hogs start rooting around for fae-touched truffles over a few generations. Alternatively: Porkabello. Porcine Porcini?

This is a 28mm scale miniature, suitable for tabletop roleplaying games such as Dungeons and Dragons or Pathfinder. No base is supplied, but is scaled to fit on a medium sized base (25.4mm / 1 inch diameter).

Rigged version of an ork made by VidovicArts. I used this to create all my ork models so far.

There are a some hidden parts in the file and lots of poses in the pose library of the rig. My workflow with this is as follows:

-Add objects like torsi an weapons to the file an pot them to the right place at the body
-hide all parts you don't need for your boi
-make copy of the rig, the body and all parts you added
-parent all objects to the rig (as objects to specific bones)
-choose a pose from the pose library or create a new one.
-apply all modifiers to the parts
-unparent all objects while keeping their transformation
-boolean unite all objects
-use windows 3D builder to repair any problems in the mesh
-print

The smallest of the 4 Gargant types the mekboy fits on the standard gw 40mm base or old monster base.

I did have some trouble printing this model on my ender 3. i found some of the bits too small and cleanup to be a pain. So i have included simplified versions of the parts that gave me the most trouble. mainly the large arm, (with or without pistons) the buzz saw (wide for PLA printers) and the grabber claw 2 or 3 fingers.
The arms can be flipped so you can swap the chain saw and guns as you like. i have made the arms quit long compaired to the origional as i never liked the stubby little arms of the metal model.
Also you can flip the big weapon mount if you want the big arm on the right side, or print one each shoulder and have a 4 armed gargant

This is inspired by the original Kev Adams 1990's era gargant with the rounded belly and arm and shoulder weapons.

some of the notable changes I made to the original design was the placement of the feed, rather than underneath they are to either side of the body, Another change was how I mounted the Buzz saw, I wanted it to look like it had a greater range of movement the 3d change was to the belly gun mount the original left huge holes in the belly that could be seen through during games, so I have added a big mantlet that I think gives the gargant a more solid look.

Also a minor tweak i widened the balcony on the back so now you can add infantry models there, but if you intend to do this do it before gluing the top body to the mid body.
With the modificatiosn its a little wider than the old model, and best mounted on a games workshop 80mm or reaper miniatures 75mm base. I have included a simple printable base id you don't have either of these sizes to hand

theoreticly you could scale this up for Titanicus, you would need to print at about 150%, priniting full size for 40k may be 2 difficult unless you cut up the hull parts or happen to have a huge print bed


You can add extra weapons from this selection here, Please mesage me if i have forgotten a weapon, i think i added all of them.

These STL files are designed to equip my [Sculptris Dummies](https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:1972042). You won't be able to import these files into Sculptris, though once you get your character posed, you can align these parts in any model staging platform (MakerBot Deskto, Blender, Meshmixer, or 3D Builder are all good choices). All of these parts are also available in Andrew Stockton's awesome [Desktop Hero](https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/263291121/desktophero-free-3d-printable-character-maker) project as well (which is quite a bit easier than adjusting all the parts by hand). All of these weapons have been scaled to 28mm/Heroic scale, so they should be ready for any kind of miniature conversion if you want to print them separately.

If you make anything with these (including through Desktop Hero), let me know and post a link here in the comments section (and certainly post a remix when you have something printable). I'd love to see what you come up with!

You can find an expanding collection of compatible parts [here](https://www.thingiverse.com/dutchmogul/collections/desktop-hero-parts).

We've set up a [Patreon page](https://www.patreon.com/illgottengames) for anyone who's interested in helping to fund us so we can keep making free and open sourced games like Pocket-Tactics, Wayfarer Tactics. and others, not to mention the growing catalog of gaming miniatures that you can use for whatever you want! (Psst... we take requests and commissions...)

Enjoy!
